newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saudis may cut barley deal to 600,000 T - traders.
newsitem.headline: Saudis may cut barley deal to 600,000 T - traders.

text.p: Saudi Arabia may reduce a major purchase of barley from the world market by 25 percent to 600,000 tonnes, European grain traders and officials said.

A week after lining up 800,000 tonnes of sales worth $130 million to the world's biggest barley importer, traders are still waiting for confirmation of the grain deals but believe the quantity may be reduced at Riyadh's request.
"The decision to reduce is apparently coming from the Saudi administration but nothing is confirmed yet," said one trader.
Reasons for a possible reduction were not clear but traders noted that barley prices have been softer recently.
Saudi Arabia provisionally bought 800,000 tonnes of barley at an August 21 tender at prices between $160 and $162 including cost, insurance and freight (CIF), traders said last week.
The grain industry has been waiting for confirmation since.
Traders have said a substantial portion of the barley is likely to come from the European Union which has both a supply and freight advantage over other producers for the time being.

But with freight costs removed, the equivalent European fob price is too low for the EU. As news of the deals emerged last week, the Commission put a floor price of some $149 per tonne fob on its barley and refused to allocate more exports just yet.
That is around seven dollars higher than the equivalent European departure price for the Saudi contract unless traders can make drastic savings on freight, operators said.
Although it is the sole realistic nearby supplier, the EU is likely to come under strong pressure this week to cover Saudi Arabia at a lower price, grain sources said on Tuesday.
An EU grain source said the Saudis were the sole big buyer in a weakening market and prices were set to fall as new crops arrived in Europe and Canada.
The EU has signalled it will release another 150,000 tonnes of German barley for export but delayed a decision last week.
